newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich defends statement on Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich defends statement on Taiwan.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Wednesday defended his warning to Chinese leaders that the United States would defend Taiwan if it was attacked, saying it was important to avoid ambiguity.

Gingrich, at a news conference with members of a congressional delegation he led to Asia, said: "As a historian, my greatest fear when you deal with a dictatorship is that ambiguity leads to a wrong understanding."

He said he had been pointing out "what was unequivocally a fact" when he warned China that the United States would defend Taiwan, which Beijing regards as a renegade province. China's foreign ministry, reacting to Gingrich's statement in Beijing, said "indiscreet remarks" by a "foreigner" were unwelcome.

Gingrich told reporters his statement reflected U.S. policy as demonstrated by the dispatch of U.S. warships to the region last year after China conducted missile tests in the Taiwan Strait and by the adoption of a House resolution of support for Taiwan.

He also announced that a bipartisan House working group to be led by Representative Doug Bereuter, a Nebraska Republican and head of a House Asia subcommittee, would be set up to monitor events after China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1.
